_comment: Video-link providers (ADR-027). ONE policy for the API (instant answer) and the worker (authoritative). status: supported = imported through an official, permitted method; needs_authorization = imported only with the user's own access token for that service; unsupported = refused with the reason and the authorised alternative. Never bypass DRM, access controls or provider terms.

providers.name: Direct link to a video file
providers.method: HTTP(S) download of the file itself, SSRF-guarded, media types only

providers.name: HLS stream playlist (.m3u8)
providers.method: Finished (VOD) playlists without encryption: every segment fetched through the SSRF guard and joined; live or encrypted streams refused

providers.name: Wikimedia Commons
providers.method: Commons API resolves the file page to the original upload; the licence and author are recorded

providers.name: Internet Archive
providers.method: Metadata API resolves the item to its original video file; the item's licence is recorded

providers.name: Dropbox shared link
providers.method: Shared links are switched to Dropbox's documented direct-download form (dl=1); links the owner has not shared fail as access denied

providers.name: Vimeo
providers.method: Vimeo API (api.vimeo.com) with the user's personal access token: only videos the API offers for download to that account (own videos, or where the owner enabled downloads)

providers.name: Google Drive
providers.method: Google Drive API (files.get, alt=media) with the user's OAuth access token for an account that can open the file

providers.name: YouTube
providers.reason: YouTube's Terms of Service allow downloading only through YouTube's own download features, and the official YouTube API offers no video-file download. OTSI VIE does not extract streams around those restrictions.
providers.alternative: If it is your video, download it from YouTube Studio (Content > ... > Download) and upload the file here. Otherwise ask the rights holder for the original file.

providers.name: Facebook / Instagram
providers.reason: Meta provides no API for third-party apps to download video files.
providers.alternative: Download your own video with Meta's 'Download your information' or the original file, and upload it.

providers.name: TikTok
providers.reason: TikTok's developer APIs do not provide video-file downloads to third-party apps.
providers.alternative: Save the original file from the creator's device or account and upload it.

providers.name: X (Twitter)
providers.reason: The X API does not offer media downloads for import into other applications under its standard terms.

providers.name: Twitch
providers.reason: Twitch's API does not provide video downloads to third-party apps.
providers.alternative: Download your VOD from the Twitch creator dashboard and upload it.

providers.name: Dailymotion
providers.reason: Dailymotion's API does not provide original-file downloads to third-party apps.

providers.name: Hudl / Wyscout / Veo
providers.reason: These are licensed football platforms; importing needs a partner integration agreement, which does not exist yet.
providers.alternative: Use the platform's own export/download for footage you hold the rights to, then upload the file.

providers.name: OneDrive / SharePoint
providers.reason: Microsoft requires a registered app and user sign-in (Microsoft Graph) for file downloads; that integration is not built yet.
providers.alternative: Download the file from OneDrive and upload it.

providers.name: Streamable
providers.reason: No official download API for third-party apps.
